I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. The size command printed 251 bytes (min+gzip) with 123 bytes of my own code in the bundle.

The exported function signatures are unchanged, and it imports only from `es-toolkit`, with no lodash import left. I did not run any input comparison against the original, so equal results on the input range are untested. Type checking against the project's `tsconfig.json` reported no errors in `out/`, though `tsc` does flag `src/module.ts` because lodash isn't installed. My own one-off `tsc --strict` run failed with `Disposable` / `AsyncDisposable` errors in es-toolkit's `.d.mts` files, which come from my ad-hoc flags, not from the migrated file.

- **`doubled`:** `mapValues` from es-toolkit, same callback.
- **`byNameKey`:** `keyBy` with `(row) => row.name`. The main es-toolkit `keyBy` takes a function, not the lodash `'name'` shorthand.
- **`toLookup`:** es-toolkit's main entry has no `fromPairs`, so this uses `zipObject` on the keys and values taken from the pairs. Duplicate names still resolve to the last value, as with lodash. The two `pairs.map` calls are the small adapter.

I also tried `fromPairs` from `es-toolkit/compat`. It bundled to 313 bytes with 95 bytes of own code. I kept `zipObject` because it gives the smaller bundle, at the cost of 28 more bytes of my own code.
